content.value_statement: Implementation work often ships without tests that prove behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through strict test-first development.
actual_capabilities: Requires a failing test before production code changes.
Guides the red, green, and refactor stages in order.
Defines checks for expected test failures and clean passing output.
Identifies common rationalizations that skip test-first work.
Links mock and test utility guidance from the included anti-patterns reference.
Provides a completion checklist for tested implementation work.
limitations: It does not choose a test framework or install dependencies.
It does not replace human approval for listed exceptions.
It assumes the project has runnable tests or a clear path to add them.
It is guidance content, not an automated test generator.

use_cases.title: Build a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Use the skill to define one expected behavior, prove it fails, then implement the smallest passing change.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Reproduce the bug with a failing test before editing the affected code path.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Discipline
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and anti-pattern reference during reviews of AI-assisted implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use strict TDD for this feature: [feature]. Identify one behavior first, write the failing test, verify the failure, then implement the minimum change.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug with a Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this TDD skill to fix this bug: [bug]. Create a failing regression test that reproduces it before changing production code.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Under Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [area] using this skill. First confirm or add behavior tests, verify they fail when needed, then keep all tests green during cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review Testing Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this implementation plan against strict TDD. Identify missing failing tests, mock anti-patterns, and the smallest safe next test to write.

output_examples.input: Implement retry behavior for a failing operation.
output_examples.output: The assistant writes a failing retry test, confirms the expected failure, adds minimal retry logic, then refactors after all tests pass.

output_examples.input: Fix empty email submissions being accepted.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a regression test for empty email input, verifies the current failure, then adds validation for that behavior.

output_examples.input: Review tests that rely heavily on mocks.
output_examples.output: The assistant flags assertions about mock elements, recommends testing real behavior, and suggests lower-level mocks only where isolation is needed.

best_practices: Write the smallest failing test before changing production code.
Verify that each failure is expected and caused by missing behavior.
Refactor only after tests pass and keep output clean.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation code first and adding tests later.
Testing mock behavior instead of real user-visible behavior.
Adding production methods that exist only to support tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI coding agents follow test-driven development for features, bug fixes, refactors, and behavior changes.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to use the project test command and verify failures and passes.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it be used with existing untested code?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends adding tests for existing behavior before new changes.

faq.question: Does it allow exceptions to TDD?
faq.answer: Only with human partner approval for cases such as throwaway prototypes, generated code, or configuration files.

faq.question: What testing mistakes does it address?
faq.answer: It addresses tests added after implementation, overuse of mocks, incomplete mocks, and test-only production methods.
